title: What If the Air Got Too Hot and Wet to Survive?

scenes.text: What if sweating stopped working? Even a fit person with water would die.
The line is a wet-bulb reading of 35 Celsius. Past it, sweat cannot evaporate fast enough to cool you.
After about six hours without cooling, the body overheats and organs can fail.
Weather stations have hit it. Gulf and Indus Valley sites topped it at least a dozen times between 1979 and 2017.
Each time lasted only about one to two hours. Far more places have reached 31 degrees, over 7,000 times worldwide.
So the limit is not a distant theory. The hottest places on Earth are already brushing it, an hour or two at a time.

description:
What if the air got so hot and humid that sweating stopped working?
A wet-bulb temperature of 35 Celsius is the survival limit, and weather stations have already touched it for an hour or two.
What should we run through next?
